what: Line Fundamentals Level 1: the range of straight strokes Rowan keeps (652 kept lines from 19 batches). A stroke is a sigma-lognormal movement drawn with a superellipse tool; the model is the stroke() function in the Line Fundamentals pages. To draw a new stroke: pick a random anchor, add Gaussian noise of the given nudge size to each setting on the 0-1 scale u (tight settings set the stroke's character, loose ones give variety), clamp to [0,1], and map u to a value with the param spec.
u_to_value: lin: lo+(hi-lo)u; log: lo*(hi/lo)^u; sq: lo+(hi-lo)u^2

params.name: Tool size
params.hint: tool radius, % of the long stroke

params.name: Movement shape
params.hint: low: even speed · high: fast launch, slow finish

params.name: Speed thinning
params.hint: 0: speed has no effect · high: fast parts thin

params.name: Pen down
params.hint: where in the movement the tool touches paper

params.name: Pen up
params.hint: where in the movement the tool leaves paper

params.name: Landing
params.hint: time to press fully down, in movement times

params.name: Lift-off
params.hint: time to lift off, in movement times

params.name: Touch pressure
params.hint: pressure at first contact and at lift

params.name: Tool angle
params.hint: chisel angle to the stroke, degrees

params.name: Timing with length
params.hint: 0: every stroke takes the same time · 1: same speed

tool_angle: relative to the page (a held pen), so a flat tool gives thick and thin parts on curves
pruned: liked lines whose redrawn versions were rejected at least half the time (2+ redraws) are left out
